title: Grounding: climb, banking, crest, compression and short jump
description: Grounding fixture from BENCHMARKS.md 'Handling fixtures' (Grounding row): 12% climb and descent, banking of +/-12 degrees, a crest, a compression and a short jump with a safe landing. Segment lengths, radii and the entry speed are authored initial values; BENCHMARKS specifies the grades, bank angles and feature set only. The jump ramp geometry (takeoff grade, airborne gap, required landing run) is undetermined and is declared null with unknowns entries rather than invented.

geometry.start_reference: World origin at the start of segment 0 on the centerline; forward -Z, right +X, up +Y.

segments.note: Authored 60 m climb at the documented 12% initial grade target.
Authored radius/angle; banking at the documented +12 degree initial target.
Crest approach; the crest feature is anchored at the end of this segment.
Descent into the compression; the compression feature is anchored at the end of this segment.
Authored radius/angle; banking at the documented -12 degree initial target.
Jump ramp approach; the jump feature is anchored at the end of this segment.
Authored trailing straight after the jump. It is an initial geometry value, not a validated landing envelope; the required landing run is declared in the jump feature as null.

features.description: Crest at the top of the climb.
Compression at the bottom of the descent.
Short jump with a safe landing, per the BENCHMARKS grounding row.
features.note: Ramp and gap geometry is M1 authoring work; no numerical jump parameters are claimed here.

runs.description: Full throttle held through climb, crest, descent, compression, banked arcs and jump; landing must preserve a usable forward direction.

initial_state.note: 25 m/s is an authored initial entry speed; BENCHMARKS specifies no entry speed for the grounding fixture.

driver.note: Single entry holds to the end of the run.

timing_gates.purpose: End of the trailing straight after landing.

expected_events.note: GAME_DESIGN: landings preserve a usable forward direction and blend back into grip; presentation suspension cannot throw the simulation body.

comparison.purpose: Behavioral grounding check across the three starters at stock and maximum upgrades: adhesion, landing recovery and grade/bank response. This is not a paired time comparison.

metrics.name: landing_forward_direction_retained
metrics.description: GAME_DESIGN requirement that landings preserve a usable forward direction; recorded and reviewed from telemetry, with no numerical threshold claimed before M1 measurements.

comparison.note: No tunneling, launching or nonfinite states are acceptable outcomes (TECHNICAL_DESIGN T04); those are motor test gates, not fixture metrics.

cars.note: BENCHMARKS handling comparisons use all three starters at stock and maximum upgrades.

unknowns.reason: Jump ramp geometry is M1 authoring work; no takeoff grade is claimed here.
The airborne gap is set by the M1 ramp geometry and validated against landing space; no value is claimed here.
The required safe landing run depends on entry speed and ramp geometry; the authored 40 m trailing straight is an initial geometry value, not a validated envelope.
car.balanced_starter is the fixed ID of the balanced starter (Comet) from BENCHMARKS; the Sparrow and Slidewinder IDs are working names until the M1 car registry assigns stable IDs.

The per-car handling resource (../handling_config.schema.json) is M1 work; the revision this fixture targets is undetermined until M1 assigns it. BENCHMARKS regenerates reference records when handling dependencies change, so the fixture records the target revision instead of duplicating coefficients.
